clue.text: Island flat where one can find space and return?

definitions.text: where one can find space and return?

blocks.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
a pad is informal for a flat or home

explanation.surface: An island apartment as a place to find room to breathe and come back to.
explanation.walkthrough: Space and return look like a holiday idea; they are the names of two keys on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A keypad carries buttons labelled space and return, so that is where those two keys are located.

clue.text: Expert in chasing work?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone skilled at hunting down jobs
setter's reading: chasing is ornamenting metal by tooling grooves into its surface

explanation.walkthrough: Chasing work sounds like job-hunting, but chasing is a metalworking craft of incising designs.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who cuts designs into metal practises chasing, the skill of tooling decorative lines.

clue.text: Part in which true friend stripped, being into that sort of thing

definitions.text: being into that sort of thing

indicators.note: stripped means the outer layer, the first and last letters, is removed
in which means the other letters are placed inside this word

blocks.note: PT is the abbreviation for part
true with its outer letters removed
friend with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A role in which a close friend undresses, for someone who enjoys that kind of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: That sort of thing is a coy euphemism for sex, the definition's hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having an excessive interest in sexual matters, which is the euphemism here.

clue.text: Fair attraction sure to have some impact

definitions.text: Fair attraction sure to have some impact

blocks.clueFragment: Fair attraction sure to have some impact
blocks.note: surface reading: a lovely-looking person who is bound to make an impression
setter's reading: a funfair ride where the little vehicles bump into each other

explanation.walkthrough: Fair attraction suggests a beautiful person; it is a ride at a funfair, and impact is literal collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper cars at a funfair are designed to collide, so physical impact is guaranteed.

clue.text: Yorkshire town's bridge team, with third person, crushing resistance; bravo!

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing tight around something, so these letters hold others inside

blocks.note: a bridge scoresheet has columns for We and They, so one partnership is We
they is a third-person pronoun
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire town's bridge team gains a third player and crushes the opposition: well done!
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge scoresheets head their columns We and They. Wetherby is a market town in West Yorkshire, known for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Wetherby is a real town in Yorkshire; the possessive 's reads as 'is' in the cryptic reading.

clue.text: Time stuck in two US heliports ruined busy holiday

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a different order
stuck in means pushed inside the other letters

blocks.note: these letters rearranged, before the time is placed
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Delays at two American heliports wreck a hectic vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra T for time sits inside the shuffled letters of two US heliports.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-stop tour packs many brief visits into a short trip, so it is a hectic holiday.

clue.text: One from Germany confined to home without energy? Unspeakable

indicators.note: without means lacking, and energy is the physics symbol E
confined to means shut up inside the other word

blocks.note: house minus its E for energy
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A German stuck at home with no energy left: too awful to talk about.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means shockingly wicked, so bad that it is unspeakable.

clue.text: Missile sent skywards in anger suits industry

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word skywards makes it read from bottom to top
in means placed inside the other word

blocks.note: rage is extreme anger
a dart is a thrown missile

explanation.surface: An angry outburst sends a dart flying up into a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Suits looks like a verb meaning pleases; it is the clothing that the industry makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is a colloquial name for the clothing industry, which makes suits among other garments.

clue.text: Old hog somehow features in nomadic home culture

indicators.note: somehow means put together in some way or other, not the given order
features in means appears inside the other word

blocks.note: a yurt is the round felt tent of Central Asian nomads
O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An old pig makes an appearance in a tent belonging to wandering herders.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghourt is milk fermented with a bacterial culture, and is commonly called a culture itself.

clue.text: Lied sung after retiring includes lyrics from liturgy

indicators.note: the words include the answer within their run of letters, so it sits inside them
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: read the run of letters from right to left and the answer lies inside

explanation.surface: A German art song, sung once a performer has stepped back, borrows words from a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Lied looks like a German song to be defined, but it is merely fodder for the backwards hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei (Lamb of God) is a prayer text from the Mass, part of the Christian liturgy.

clue.text: Flirtatious girl, bubbly sounding, going out regularly

indicators.note: sounding means the word is to be taken by how it is pronounced
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

blocks.note: something bubbly has fizz; spelt with one Z here
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A flirty young woman, sparkling as she heads out for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizgig is an old word for a frivolous, flirtatious young woman.

clue.text: Plain policy document the last to go

indicators.note: the final letter is to be dropped from the word

blocks.note: a party's published statement of policy

explanation.surface: A plain policy statement with the last item cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective describing the document, but it is the definition, meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest as an adjective means clearly evident, which is a sense of plain.

clue.text: Hack back working following twenty-four hours in Paris

indicators.note: back means the following word is read in the backward direction
following means this piece comes after the one named next, so it goes second

blocks.note: jour is French for day
working is ON, read backwards

explanation.surface: A reporter gets back to work after a day in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a slang term for a jobbing reporter, and journo is the informal word for a journalist.

clue.text: Pearly courtesan dancing short tango

indicators.note: short of tango means lacking the letter that tango stands for in the phonetic alphabet
dancing letters move about and settle in a new order

blocks.note: courtesan with its T removed, since tango is T

explanation.surface: A pearl-wearing courtesan performs an abbreviated tango.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, so nacreous describes the pearly, iridescent sheen.

clue.text: Waterworks specialist runs over record kept by Hebridean isles

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the word that follows

blocks.note: North and South Uist are islands in the Outer Hebrides
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A plumber on a Scottish island keeps a log of how water flows.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterworks is British slang for the urinary system, so the specialist is a doctor, not a plumber.
explanation.definitionFit: A urologist is the doctor who treats the urinary tract, jokingly called the waterworks.

clue.text: Curse of Dark Arts every now and again?

indicators.note: every now and again means picking letters at intervals, every other one

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A wizard's curse drawn from the Dark Arts, used only occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: Curse looks like a spell, which fits the Dark Arts; here it is the mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Drat is a mild exclamation of annoyance, a minor curse or oath.

clue.text: Urbane dweeb intermittently transmitting live

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so only alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
a programme going out live is on air

explanation.surface: A suave nerd whose broadcast keeps cutting in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave, charming and stylish, which is a close synonym for urbane.

clue.text: The so-called greatest compilers eschewing film VIPs

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the named part is left out

blocks.note: the boxer Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest
crossword compilers are setters
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: The supposed top crossword setters shun movie celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: The so-called greatest looks like a description of the compilers, but it is the boxer's self-awarded nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A-listers are the top-tier celebrities, the most important people in a field.

clue.text: Page engaged by established Irish clan

indicators.note: engaged by means taken on and held within the other word

blocks.note: set means fixed or established
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A page boy hired by a long-standing Irish family.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a branch or clan of an Irish family group.

clue.text: Sheik evacuated flying alpine transporter

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outer letters remain
flying letters scatter and land in a new arrangement

blocks.note: sheik emptied of its inner letters
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sheik flies off in a mountain transport after clearing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski-plane is an aircraft fitted with skis for landing on snow, a means of transport.

clue.text: Discount 100 different picture frames

indicators.note: different means the word is made into something else by rearranging
frames means surrounds the other letter like a frame

blocks.note: picture with its letters rearranged
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A hundred off on various picture frames in a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A price cut is a reduction in what something costs, which is a discount.

clue.text: Worry with gold finish of Lübeck ornamental carving

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to fret is to worry
W is the abbreviation for with
or is gold in heraldry
the last letter of the German city's name

explanation.surface: Fretting over gilded decoration at the end of a trip to Lübeck.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretwork is decorative openwork cut or carved into wood in an interlaced pattern.

clue.text: Fleetingly fashionable, fine hotel outside northern part of African capital

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around the other piece

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the first part of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia's capital, as written in a down entry

explanation.surface: A smart hotel on the north side of an African capital, briefly in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the first word of the city's name sits at the top, so northern.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddish describes something that is a passing craze, popular only briefly.

clue.text: Edison having broken leg

indicators.note: a broken word has its letters smashed and rearranged

blocks.note: the inventor's name taken as written

explanation.surface: The inventor Edison has fractured a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, the half behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, leg and on side are two names for the same half of the field.

clue.text: Survey potential client

blocks.note: first meaning: to explore an area for minerals, or a view surveyed
second meaning: a likely future customer

explanation.surface: Researching a possible new customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospect means a sweeping view or to explore land, and also a person who may become a customer.

clue.text: Excellent starters of teriyaki, if considerably vinegary

indicators.note: starters means the opening letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: ace is slang for excellent
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Delicious teriyaki appetisers, if they are rather sour.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters looks like the first course of a meal, fitting the Japanese teriyaki; here it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the main component of vinegar, so acetic describes something vinegary.

clue.text: Member of ruling clique occasionally moulding curved structure

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
an arch is a curved structure spanning an opening

explanation.surface: A powerful insider occasionally shaping a curved building.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of the small group of people who hold power in an oligarchy.

clue.text: Jam session of maybe sixty minutes?

explanation.walkthrough: Jam session suggests musicians improvising; the words split into a traffic jam and a frantic hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The rush hour is the busy commuting period when roads are congested, a period of roughly an hour of hurry.

clue.text: Doctor final part of Treasury agreement

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: to doctor is to give medical treatment
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fiddling the end of a Treasury deal.
